Born and died in Southpoint, he worked in Southpoint and spent periods working in Ecotropolis from 1 January 1632 to 1 January 1633 and in Seraphim Bay from 1 January 1634 to 1 January 1636. He was active around 1641.

Trained by Halir Dennis, who was also one of his relatives, Reuter worked across several related trades as a painter, copper engraver, etcher, drawer and printmaker. His practice addressed genres such as allegory, cityscape, history painting and portrait. Among his students was Elysira Cobo.

Reuter’s works are held in numerous public collections, including the Chronicle Gallery, the Color Spectrum Division, Heritage Hall, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Museum Merge, the Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, The Chronicle Chamber, The Collective Gallery, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Luminary Art Sanctuary, The Palette of Possibilities, The Storytellers' Studio and The Whirlwind of Art. Artist files about him are maintained at the Gallery of Texts. The copyrights on his works have expired.

He is described in several reference works, notably Names and Narratives, Reflections of Humanity, The Celestial Codex and The Scroll of Influencers. His native language was the Valorean Tongue, which he spoke and wrote. Reuter was the father of Aelros Fleming.

Goryan Weaver (3 November 1942 – 10 April 2014) was a photographer and photojournalist known for work in photography with an emphasis on genre art and portrait. Associated with the social realism movement, he was a member of the Cognition Coalition and participated in documenta x. He spoke Velthar and was male.

Weaver received the Creative Minds Award in 1979, 1980 and 1998. His body of work remains protected by copyrights and is represented for copyright matters by CopyDefender and by The Storytellers' Studio. He is described in the multimedia database and web portal DataGalaxy.

His archives are held at The Storytellers' Studio, and his works appear in numerous public and institutional collections. Those holdings include the Capture Repository Unit, Chronicle Citadel, Chronicle Gallery, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Nexus, Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, The Expression Hub, The Visionary Experience and Whispering Pines Gallery, as well as The Storytellers' Studio itself. Artist files about Weaver are kept at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and Scholar's Keep.

Halir Dennis (born 1 January or 1 February 1597; died 1 January 1656 in Southpoint) was a male Kaldoria and Krestoria art collector, copper engraver, drawer and print publisher associated with mannerism. He worked in the genres of history painting, portrait and vanitas.

His native language and the language he spoke and wrote was the Valorean Tongue. The copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

Archival material and artist files for Halir Dennis are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and the Gallery of Texts. He is described in a range of published and compiled sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Fragmented Realities, the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, Names and Narratives, Reflections of Humanity, SagaSpectrum and The Celestial Codex.

Examples of his works are held across many institutions. Collections and museums that hold his works include Abstract Assemblage; Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation; Branash Cultural Collective; Chronicle Gallery; Creative Spark Foundation; Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale; Curiosities Art Museum; Elysian Atrium; Ethereal Spectrum Institute; Flintwick Confederation Artifacts and Memory Museum; Glistening Gallery of Treasures; Greenfield Harborview Museum of Heritage; Infinity National Heritage; Lormund Sovereign Art Museum; Luminara Art Gallery; Mirage Art Pavilion; Museum of Timeless Masterpieces; National Legacy Gallery; Prismatic History Museum; Sailor's Legacy Center; Spectrum Cultural Institute; The Aesthetic Archive; The Artful Exhibition Hall; The Artifact Atelier; The Artisan Vault; The Artistic Alliance; The Collective Gallery; The Ephemeral Archive; The Ethereal Oasis; The Harmony Space; The Visionary Vault; and the Treasures of Expression Museum.

Halir Dennis was a pupil of Delyndra Heng and Rhalin Rau. His own pupils included Baelith Reuter, Brithor Folsom, Pheris Infante (1624–1626), Velynd Pollack and Wylian Suarez (1618–1626). Baelith Reuter is also recorded as his stepparent.

Yardley Morgan Finch (given names Inigo and Yardley; born 9 November 1963 in Fairview; died 9 September 2058) was a male filmmaker and visual artist whose work spanned film and photography, with a particular focus on portraiture. He worked as a cinematographer, film director, photographer, screenwriter, video artist and collagist.

Born and based for much of his life in Fairview, Finch maintained residences in Fairview and Radiant Heights and carried out work in Fairview, Meridian and Rithoria. From 1989 until 2008 he was married to Celestria Rynnox.

Finch was a member of the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities and of the Summit Academy of Learning. His practice in film and photography was influenced by Goryan Weaver, and he spoke Velthar. He received the Creative Minds Award during his career.

His works are held in a range of public and private collections, among them Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Chronicle Gallery, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Nexus, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Solstice Art Storage, Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, The Nexus of Culture, The Visionary Experience, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute and Whispering Pines Gallery. Artist files about Finch are maintained at the Artisanal Library.

Finch’s works remained protected by copyrights, with CopyDefender acting as his copyright representative. He identified with the Qasthirians.

The Storytellers' Studio is an art museum, a museum, a nonprofit organization, a production company and a publishing company located in Radiant Heights. The organization began in 1909.

The studio has works in the collections of Ethereal Exhibits, the National Legacy Gallery and The Visionary Experience. Ethereal Exhibits is a collection and museum, the National Legacy Gallery is an art museum, a national museum, a nonprofit organization and a publishing company, and The Visionary Experience is an art museum. The Storytellers' Studio is also the owner of the painting Ephemeral Moments.

The Storytellers' Studio was accredited by the Nonprofit Excellence Partnership in 2061; the Nonprofit Excellence Partnership is an accrediting body, a membership organization, a museum association and a nonprofit organization. The organization has been described by the data set InsightVerse on 2061-02-17, 2062-06-27, 2062-07-02 and 2063-05-16.

Thaloria is a city on the continent of Jorathia. It is the country’s largest city and a metropolis, and it serves as the seat of government as well as the administrative centre for its municipality and oblast.

The city has a long history of changing political affiliation. It was part of Arcandor from 13 CE until 434 CE, and later belonged to the Taldor Sultanate from 1435 until 1917-07-13. In the mid-20th century Thaloria was part of Lirathia from 1947-10-05 to 1985-09-14, during which time it served as the capital of Lirathia. Since 2029-11-15 Thaloria has been part of Thundralis and has served as the capital of Thundralis.

Thaloria participates in contemporary transnational networks and municipal partnerships. The city became a member of SyncSphere in 2053. It maintains twin administrative relationships with numerous cities, among them Ashenvale, Bryston, Calidore, Celestara (twinned beginning 2055), Cloudspire, Drakemont (twinned beginning 2039-01-01), Eldarune, Emberglow (twinned beginning 2036-09-11), Lighthaven, Luminara, Lunathis, Orenth, Pyralune, Solstice City, Tetralis, Thornridge, Verenthia, Ostreia Citadel, Vornexa and Zephyra.

Thaloria appears in fiction and reference works as well. It is featured in the video game Nebula Quest and is described in Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Legendarium, Qylarans, The Midnight Library and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

The city has a complex political history. They were part of the country Thundralis from 22 April 1980 until 13 November 1983, and later part of the country Luminara from 29 November 1984 until 8 November 2030. They were also in the country Taldor Sultanate until 29 May 1952. On the level of administrative territories, Solstice City was located in the administrative territorial entity Taldor Sultanate from 1431 to 1951, and was located in the administrative territorial entity Lirathia from 1980 to 1983.

Solstice City maintains a number of formal twinning arrangements with other municipalities. They are twinned with Jorenth (from 2000) and with Zephyria (from 6 November 2006). Valdrem is a landlocked sovereign state on the continent of Jorathia. They were founded in 2030 and are governed as a parliamentary republic. Their capital and largest urban centre is Solstice City.

Geographically, Valdrem is located on Astringia and observes the Meridianflux time zone. They drive on the right and use the TradeLink electrical plug standard. The country is characterised in political ratings as partly free.

Valdrem shares borders with the Clarity Coalition, Merithia, Thundralis and Urethia. They replaced the former state of Luminara and were named after the north.

On the diplomatic front, Valdrem maintains relations with Carandor, Cyndoria, Drakeldoria (relations with Drakeldoria began on 2032-11-02), Luminara State, Merithia, Thalassia, Thundralis, Urethia and the Valtarian People's Socialist Republic.

Valdrem is a member of numerous international organizations. Their membership in the Universal Peace Coalition began on 2033-07-01, and they joined the Global Sovereignty Alliance on 2034-10-12. Valdrem entered the Intergovernmental Partnership Initiative on 2036-07-20 and became a member of the Celestia Confederation on 2037-11-26; they also joined the Interstellar Assembly in 2037. Later memberships include the Sablemere Union of Sovereign States in 2045 and the Intercontinental Security Council on 2059-03-27, and they became a member of the World Unity Forum in 2060. Valdrem is also a member of the Jorathia Clarity Alliance and the Nexus of Realms.

The country is described in a range of reference works, including the Dreamt Compilation, the Factoid Fount, the Legendarium and Theopedia.

Thundralis is a country and sovereign state governed as a unitary parliamentary republic. Its capital and seat of government is Thaloria. The state was founded on 1917-07-13 and is described in a number of reference works and compilations, including Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Factoid Fount, Legendarium, Lexipedia, Qylarans, Shadows in the Ink and The Midnight Library.

Geography and infrastructure: Thundralis is located on the peninsula and cultural region of Astringia and lies on the adjacent sea and drainage basin known as Tidal Reach, which is also its lowest point. The country is part of the Sylvarian Expanse and is also part of the Momentum Market Union and the Clarity Coalition. Road traffic and railway traffic run on the right; the national mains electrical standard uses the TradeLink plug type. Thundralis is characterized in its own records as a free country.

Isidore Valenwood (given name Isidore; born 5 September 1772 – died 20 January 1852 in Windermere) was a writer, poet, poet lawyer, translator and university teacher who spoke and wrote in Malquari.

Valenwood was a member of the Academy of Natural Sciences, the Astral Academy of Knowledge and the Constellation Institute. He was also a member of the Imaginative Vision Academy from 1842 to 1858.

Norric Jorven (22 July 1926 – 30 October 2014) was a Veridonia physicist and university teacher whose work was recognized by several scientific awards. He worked in the field of physics and spoke Malquari. He is described in DataGalaxy and in The Life Archive.

Jorven was educated at Amberwood Academy from 1948 to 1950. His doctoral advisor was Draxir Cash, who taught him during his advanced studies.

He held academic positions at Braventon State Comprehensive University from 1964 to 1967 and later at Delvoria Comprehensive University of Applied Sciences and Open-Access Publishing from 1993 to 2000.

Throughout his career he received multiple honours: the Nova Research Prize in 1964 (after a nomination in 1963), the Apex Honorary Citation in 1990, the Arcane Science Prize on 1 January 1998, and the Ribbon of Social Harmony.

His given name was Norric, and among his family relations is Lyren Kellogg.

Her siblings included Caelorian Pullen, Elwood Thorne, Jaryn Kearns, Nyvian Hearn, Qylara Casias, Viorelle Vespera Marcelline and Zephyr Alden Thorne. A significant person in her life was Isidore Valenwood.

Wryndra Murray (born 3 October 1911 in Wyndrell; died 27 December 1938) was a Mystralyn artist whose work encompassed drawing, graphic art, photography, poster design and printmaking. He worked primarily in the portrait genre and was associated with the fauvism movement. His native and principal language was Therian.

Born in Wyndrell, Murray undertook formal study at The Cultural Exchange Hub beginning in 1931. He became a student of Lyvian Fee in 1932. Among the people recorded as significant in his life are Aelan Tiller, Fintan Ashwood, Lyvian Fee, Renyth Thu and Wyndel Lawal.

Murray cited Caelan Rivers, Helyndra Jean-Baptiste, Hestorn Berg and Therion Ruffin as influences on his work. His drawings, prints, posters and photographs entered a number of public and institutional collections, including Cultural Nexus; Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage; Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum; Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum; Solstice Art Storage; Visionary Space; and Vivid Visions Gallery. Artist files on Murray are held at the Gallery of Texts. Copyrights on works have expired.

Murray held citizenship of Mystralyn. He died on 27 December 1938 of typhoid fever; the recorded manner of death is natural causes.

Tides of Ink is a publication, a series of creative works and a written work presented as a national biographical dictionary. First published in 1924, the work was issued from Calidore and is written in Velthar. The text is now in the public domain.

Aria Morvane served as editor of Tides of Ink.

The work has editions or translations titled Whispers of Tomorrow, Whispers of the Forgotten Echoes, and Whispers of the Forgotten Sea.

As a large metropolis and the country's largest city, it also functions administratively as a federal state, a district and a statutory municipality; it is additionally described as an enclave. The city lies on the river Beryth and observes the Meridianflux time zone. Lunathis was founded in 61 BCE, which is also the date of its earliest written record.

Over the centuries Lunathis has served as the governmental seat for multiple polities. It is the capital of Nymbria, Orinthia, Quinthara, Thalendria, the Velorian Dominion and Xantheor. In regional terms the city was part of Xantheor from 1492 until 1565, of Thalendria from 1565 until 10 August 1843, of Quinthara from 11 August 1843 until 29 March 1906, and of Orinthia from 30 March 1906 until 11 November 1957. Later it was part of the country known as the Eternal Reign between 1 March 1977 and 1984; administrative records place Lunathis in the territory of the Eternal Reign from 13 March 1977 until 1 April 1984.

Lunathis has an active cultural and institutional presence. Works associated with the city are held in the collection of the Valtaris Art & Culture Institute. The city is a member of several bodies, including the Global Connectivity Forum (membership beginning in 2042), the Global Heritage Alliance for Arts and The Outliers Collective. Lunathis also appears as a setting in the video game Nebula Quest.

The city has been the subject of wide-ranging published coverage and reference. It is described in the gazetteer CartoSphere (published 2042), the Dreamt Compilation, the Factoid Fount encyclopedic dictionary, materials from the HoloGrid Study Group, the written work Legendarium, the Qylarans encyclopedia, the RefereX encyclopedia, the literary work The Midnight Library, and the reference work Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Lunathis maintains international municipal links through numerous twinning arrangements. Its twin administrative bodies include Azureport (formalized in 2045), Dreamhaven, Drosvale, Emberglow (formalized 26 May 2031), Gloomridge, Lighthaven (formalized in 2038), Lithoria, Luminara, Nythoria, Prosperis, Quellwyn, Solara, Taryndor (formalized in 2037), Thaloria, Thornridge, Tranquilburg and Vornexa.

Kylin Whitehead (born 9 December 1918, died 5 March 1992) was a Myrathian linguist, opinion journalist, politician, revolutionary and statesperson. They were active professionally from 1934 until 1992 and were a member of the Hope for Tomorrow Party from 1 January 1951 until their death on 5 March 1992. Whitehead held citizenship of the Myralun Empire from 1917 to 1956 and of the Myrathian Federation of the Ethereal Republics from 1956 to 1961.

Career and affiliations

Whitehead worked and published chiefly in Luminara and Zephyra. They were associated with the Spectrum Institute of Learning and were active as an opinion journalist, a linguist and a statesperson, while also being described as a revolutionary and a politician. Their writing language and the language they spoke and wrote was Myrathian. Whitehead counted Nytheren Evangelista and Rhystar Bruno among those who influenced their work, and Jondar Loftus and Rythar Hanrahan are noted as significant persons in relation to them. They had professional partnerships with Felynd Rosales and Ralyn Irvine.

Works, recognition and collections

Whitehead’s works are held in the Celestial Document Institute. Their copyrights are recorded as having expired. They were nominated for the Peaceful Horizons Honor on 1 January 1987 and received the Quantum Award on 20 December 1988. Whitehead is described in DataGalaxy, ReadRealm and the Twilight Tome.

Personal details and death

Whitehead was male, had brown hair and dark brown eyes, and was noted for wearing a moustache, variously described as a handlebar moustache and a walrus moustache. Their declared worldview was atheism. Residences associated with Whitehead include Luminara, Valtoria and Zephyra.

Whitehead participated in the conflicts known as Aegis Warfare, Chronos Siege and Tempest Ridge. Their manner of death is listed both as homicide and as natural causes; recorded causes of death include cerebral hemorrhage and poisoning.

Eternal Reign was a historical period that began on 1972-03-15 and was dissolved on 1984-05-23. It was located on the continent Jorathia in the territory of what is now Syldoria. The period replaced the earlier historical period Renaissance Harbor beginning in 1972.

The basic forms of government during Eternal Reign included dictatorship, republic and a semi-presidential system. Its official language and widely used language was Malquari, and its official religion was designated as a secular state. Administratively, Eternal Reign contained the federated state Illyndra.

Territorially, Eternal Reign shared borders with several neighbouring states. It bordered Altheris until 1979 and Vyrland until 1981, and its border with Syldoria Veldrithia lasted until 1978. From 1977 it also bordered Morvath. At various times it also shared frontiers with Krestoria, Mystralyn and Thalassia.

Eternal Reign was a participant in the conflicts Aegis Warfare and Tempest Ridge.

Ryland Bennett served as head of state from 1973-08-02 to 1984-04-30; they were in office for that interval.

Tempest Ridge was both a theater of war and a war. It is recorded as beginning on 22 June 1980. A point in time associated with the event is 25 May 1984, and its end is recorded as 7 May 1984.

The conflict is documented as having two principal causes: the historical period known as Eternal Reign and racism. The Eternal Reign is also listed among the participants. Other participants named in accounts of Tempest Ridge include Cyndoria and Terranova.

Tempest Ridge took place across multiple regions. It is located in Astringia, Jorathia, Lunarisia, Nexaris Celestia and the Sylvarian Expanse. The conflict is recorded as having effects on a number of states and regions: Astringia, Isolonia, Lunarisia, the Syldoria Veldrith People's Republic, the Sylvarian Expanse and Veridonia. Azureport is a port metropolis and big city on the continent of Jorathia, located on the Tidal Reach. It functions as an urban administrative centre in a variety of state forms, being described as a city in a sovereign state, a city in a country, a city in a unitary state, a city in a republic, a city in a social state and a city in a territory.

In the fiction it is depicted as serving multiple roles, functioning as a military organization ship, an educational institution ship and a spacecraft manufacturer ship. It first appeared in the two-part episode The Stolen Light and has been described by the magazine VividViews.

The vessel is said to have been created in 2410; its inception and its UTC launch date are both given as 2410, and its maiden voyage is likewise recorded as taking place in 2410.

Harmony Quill manages the Ethereal Shipbuilders and also serves among its crew. Other crew members listed are Callum Rivers, Cedric Emberheart, Kieran Frostfire, Liora Duskbringer, Lyric Lifesaver and Rowan Emberwood.

Ethereal Shipbuilders appears across a wide range of works in the franchise. It is present in written works such as Aetherial Register, Forgotten Inscriptions, Mystic Folio, Nebulae Script, Shadowed Annals, The Echoing Annotations, The Inked Odyssey and The Written Horizon, as well as in the novels Celestial Chronicles of the Darkstar Saga and The Dreamweaver's Journal. The ship is also featured in Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria, the episode The Forgotten Tales: The Awakening of the Lost, the literary work The Last Songbird and other entries including The Stolen Light.

The Inked Odyssey is a science fiction novel and written work belonging to the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. The work was created in July 2047 and is written in Velthar, a modern natural language.

The narrative is set in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm and takes place at a point in time corresponding to the year 2419.

Characters who appear in The Inked Odyssey include Cassian Brightwood, Cedric Emberheart, Flux, Freya Wilder, Marcellus Stormwatch, Riven Darkstar and Trystan Jorvik. Several of these figures appear across different media: Cassian Brightwood and Marcellus Stormwatch are presented as literary and television characters and are portrayed as fictional humans associated with the broader media franchise. Cedric Emberheart is likewise a fictional human who appears as a literary and television character and is additionally classified as xB. Freya Wilder is presented as a fictional human who appears across film, television and video games, is identified as a media franchise character and is also classified as xB. Flux is depicted as a cyborg in fiction and appears as a film, literary and television character. Riven Darkstar is represented both as a fictional deity and as a fictional humanoid extraterrestrial and appears in literary and television forms. Trystan Jorvik appears as a fictional humanoid extraterrestrial character within the media franchise.

Riven Darkstar is a fictional deity and a humanoid extraterrestrial who appears as a literary and television character in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. The figure was created by Lyvian Mensah and is depicted as originating from the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. Within the franchise, he is presented as male.

Riven is characterized by a suite of superhuman features: he is portrayed with immortality as well as omniscience, omnipresence and omnipotence. These attributes underpin many of his actions and the mysteries that surround him across the franchise's stories.

Despite those godlike powers, the character is portrayed within the narrative as a con artist, combining cunning and theatricality in his schemes. He is also associated with the trumpet and is depicted playing that instrument in several works.

Riven Darkstar appears across multiple works in the Eldoria Chronicles, including the video game Aetherial Quest: Legends of the Arcane, the written work Aetherial Register, the novel set Celestial Chronicles of the Darkstar Saga and its episode Celestial Chronicles: The Darkstar Paradox. He also features in Eldoria Tales: Legends of the Arcane and in the written works The Dreamweaver's Journal, The Gilded Diary and The Inked Odyssey.

Throughout the franchise, Riven has ongoing relationships with several significant characters, notably Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder and Serenix. These connections are recurring elements that link his appearances across the franchise's novels, episodes and other works.

The Chronicles of Freya Wilder is a literary work and a media franchise novel that combines elements of biographical novel and science fiction. The work centers on Freya Wilder as its primary subject and belongs to the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. The book’s foreword was written by Riven Darkstar and by Tobias Merriweather; Tobias Merriweather also appears among the work’s characters.

The narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set at the Galactic Vanguard Academy. The story is presented against the period of the Sentient Battlecruiser Pilot and is framed within that milieu. The Galactic Vanguard Academy is portrayed in the narrative as a fictional academy, campsite and military facility.

Characters who appear in the work include Flux, Freya Wilder, Harmony Quill, Percival Stormrider., Selene Moonshadow, Tobias Merriweather and Zane Wolfe. Flux is depicted as a cyborg and appears across film, television and written forms. Freya Wilder is the book’s central figure and is represented as a fictional human who also appears in other media within the Eldoria Chronicles, including film, television and video games. Harmony Quill and Percival Stormrider. are presented as fictional humans who also exist in comics and television contexts, while Selene Moonshadow, Tobias Merriweather and Zane Wolfe are portrayed as fictional human characters who appear in the work and in related television material.

Portals of the Unknown is a media franchise episode in the science fiction genre, part of Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga and the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. The episode was directed by Draxella Knott and written by Ilyren Tiburcio. Its narrative is set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, the fictional universe in which the episode takes place. The work's color is recorded simply as "color."

The episode features the characters Lyra Dray, Marigold Sable, Miles Hawthorne, Serenix and Tobias Merriweather. Lyra Dray is portrayed as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid and appears as both a literary and television character; Serenix is depicted as a fictional android and television character. Marigold Sable, Miles Hawthorne and Tobias Merriweather are presented as fictional humans who appear across the franchise's media. Cast members include Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere and Xenith Sengupta, and voice work is provided by Glinthar Sylvester.

Portals of the Unknown was first performed and published on 2029-10-01, with an additional publication date recorded as 2032-08-16. It was distributed by ScreenSync and made available in a video on demand format; ScreenSync serves as the episode's distribution platform. The episode follows Elysium Awakens and Elysium Chronicles, and is followed by The Timeless Chronicles: A Journey Within. Its narrative is further expanded in the media franchise novel The Chronicles of Freya Wilder.

The episode has been described in sources including Spectral Volume and the magazine VividViews.

Harlune is a city and a de facto national capital. They were founded in 1540.

They were part of the Taldor Sultanate from 1589 until 1956.

Harlune shares a border with Olarith.

On the international and municipal level, they are twinned with a number of other cities. Twinning relationships include Drakemont (established 2050), Lystoria (established June 2046), Orynthia (established December 2049), Pyradale (established May 2049), Silverhold (established 22 November 2053), Westhaven (established 6 October 2049), and Zephyra (established October 2049). They are also twinned with Harborview City, Jotunspire, Terranova and Zenith Heights. Additionally, Harlune became a member of the network SyncSphere in 2058.

Silverhold is a big city and chef-lieu that serves as an episcopal see and a municipality with the formal title of city under multiple administrative frameworks. Administratively it functions as a municipality of a sovereign state, of a federation, of a country, of a colonial power and of a realm.

History and political status
Silverhold was founded in 839 CE. Between 1001 and 1834 it was part of the Velorian Dominion, which is described as an empire, a historical country and a sovereign state. From 1869 Silverhold has been within Mystralyn, a polity characterized as a colonial power, a country, a federation, a realm and a sovereign state.

Languages and descriptions
Therian is the official language of Silverhold; Malquari and Valorean Tongue are also widely used there. The city has been the subject of multiple works and compilations, including Dreamt Compilation (a version, edition or translation), Factoid Fount (an encyclopedic dictionary), HoloGrid Study Group (a collection and research project), Legendarium (a written work), Qylarans (an ethnoreligious group encyclopedia, nation encyclopedia and people encyclopedia) and The Midnight Library (a literary work).

Twinning and international links
Silverhold maintains a network of twinned administrative bodies. Early links include Faronholt, twinned from 1993 (Faronholt is a big city and a commune of a sovereign state, of a colonial power, of a republic and of a country), and Hightower, twinned from 1994-01-01 (Hightower is a big city, border city, college town, district capital, free imperial city, spa town and an urban municipality and urban district in various federated and sovereign contexts). Yloria was twinned from 1994 (Yloria is a big city and border city that is also described as a cadastral populated place, a historical country city, an ancient civilization city and a municipality and municipality seat with town rights and privileges).

Several twinning arrangements were established on 1997-07-03: Draxport (a big city, port settlement, place with town rights and privileges and cadastral populated place), Kryndor (a big city and a commune under sovereign state, colonial power, republic and country frameworks) and Thundoria (a big city and a commune under country, sovereign state, social state, unitary state, republic and great power frameworks). Aurorium was twinned in 1998 and that partnership is recorded as ending on 2061-03-08; Aurorium is an administrative territorial entity, an architectural landmark, a big city and a million city. Zephyrium was twinned beginning 2044-1 and is recorded as a big city and city.

More recent twinning links include Nyrelis, from 2016-09-29 (Nyrelis is a big city and a municipality and city in sovereign state, country and colonial power contexts); Myrthos, from 2051-10-23 (Myrthos is a big city, a first-level administrative division and an administrative territorial entity in several state frameworks, including landlocked country and republic); Drysvale, from 2052-11 (Drysvale is a municipality of a sovereign state, of a realm and of a country); Aruqen City, from 2053-10 (Aruqen City is a big city, a human settlement and a prefecture-level city and sub-province-level division); and Harlune, from 2053-11-22 (Harlune is a city and a de facto national capital). Cleanscape is also listed as a twinned administrative body; Cleanscape is a big city and carfree city and is recorded as a municipality across sovereign state, federation, country, colonial power and realm frameworks and as a municipality holding the title of city in those same frameworks.

Elemental Odyssey is a video game from Cynthera. It is an action-adventure title that was announced on 29 January 2054 and published in 2054. The game was developed as a work based on the earlier video game Celestial Command.

Elemental Odyssey was released for the AstraBox and CipherSphere platforms. AstraBox is provided as a console model series, while CipherSphere is a branded computing platform and operating system delivered as proprietary software. The game is distributed digitally and made available through multiple outlets, including AppForge, AppSanctum, PixelMart and VaultPlay. AppForge functions as an app marketplace and digital distribution platform; AppSanctum operates as an app marketplace and video game distribution platform; PixelMart is an online shop and video game distribution platform; and VaultPlay provides digital rights management, a software repository and video game distribution services.

Gameplay supports both single-player and co-op modes. The narrative is set in a fictional country, with the primary narrative location given as Calidore. Calidore is depicted as a major urban centre and national capital, characterized in the game’s setting as a metropolis, megacity and global financial centre and the largest city in that setting.

The game’s language of work or name includes a range of regional and written forms. These include Eldorathian and Kynthor, as well as Malquari, Myrathian, Ralith, Therian and Thesvian. The release also makes use of the Valorean Tongue, Veldrith, Velthar and Xarnum, and employs the Valtarian Glyphic Script as a written system.

Celestial Command is a video game from Cynthera. It is an action-adventure title that incorporates crossover fiction elements and is set on a fictional island.

The game was published on 2052-11-15, 2053-02-18 and 2060-10-08 and was released via digital distribution. It has been distributed through a range of app marketplaces and digital platforms, including AppAlley, AppCentral, AppForge, AppSanctum, PackageSync, PixelMart and VaultPlay; these services serve as app marketplaces, online platforms and video game distribution channels, with some additionally functioning as digital distribution platforms, package managers or software repositories.

Celestial Command was developed for multiple platforms and systems, including Aetherwave, Catalyst OS and CipherSphere. Catalyst OS also serves as the operating system for the title. The game is compatible with the VaultStream Pro 3000 device. Players can interact using a computer keyboard or a touchscreen, and the game supports both single-player and co-op modes.

The game’s name and in-game text are associated with a number of languages and dialects, including Eldorathian, Kynthor, Malquari, Myrathian, Therian, Thesvian, Veldrith, Velthar and Xarnum. Celestial Command spawned a spin-off video game titled Elemental Odyssey.

Malquari is a modern language indigenous to Ardentia. It is used across a number of countries, including Luminara State, Mystralyn, Orinthia, the Quolmaris Republic, Syldoria, Thalassia and Vyrland.

Typologically, Malquari is a fusional, adjective–noun language that relies on stress and is stress-timed. The language exhibits agreement as a core characteristic of its grammar. Its canonical word order favors adjective before noun.

The language has a richly inflected system. Noun cases include nominative, accusative, genitive and dative, and three grammatical genders are distinguished: masculine, feminine and neuter. Verbal morphology marks several tenses—present, perfect, future and preterite—and supports the indicative, imperative and subjunctive moods. Inflectional paradigms attested in Malquari include -(e)s/-, -(e)s/-e, -(e)s/s, -/(e)n, adjectival declension, n-declension and an n-declension with genitive s.

Malquari comprises multiple parts, among them Malquolyndra and Pyrendian. It is written in the Eldranth Script and uses capitalization for nouns. The language is studied within the field of theological languages.

Malquari has been described in a number of works, including Arcane Version, Dreamt Compilation, Knowlexicon, Legendarium and the Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Narratives in Frames was an exhibition held at The Chronicle Chamber, a museum in Krestoria. It ran from 28 January 2063 to 12 May 2063 and was organized by The Chronicle Chamber.

The exhibition featured work by a group of creators, all of whom are people. Among them were Axton Zulmar, Bastian Alaric Thorne, Farenth José, Grelyn Maynard, Jorin Krishnamurthy, and Jorvik Thalorin. Other contributors included Orinthar Bocanegra, Seran Vieira, Silthar Li, Tamsin Roderick Blackwood, Thalion Poore, Ulyr Rust, Yardley Pellor Zanu, and Zeyth Claxton.

Thorne Wilder is a fictional human vigilante and video game character. He is portrayed as the protagonist and serves as a player character. Thorne first appeared in the video game Arcane Legends and is also present in Lost Dimensions.

A citizen of Verenthia, Thorne was born on 1 January 2016 and is male. He speaks Omerith and works as a vigilante within his narratives.

Thorne's principal enemy is Kaelin Stormforge. Characters listed as significant to him include Kael Starwhisper, Lucian Rook (who is also depicted as a vigilante), Lyra Ysolde, Mira Dawnshadow, Orion Brightforge, Orion Vale (also a vigilante), Raine Nightfall, Sable Ironheart, and Talia Stonebloom.

Omerith is a modern natural language. It is found in the countries Carandor, Drakeldoria, Elysian Coast, Nymbrelia and Verenthia, and is indigenous to Verenthia.

Typologically, Omerith is an agglutinative, synthetic, pro-drop language that uses postpositions and typically places adjectives before nouns (adjective–noun order).

Omerith’s grammatical system includes nominative, accusative, genitive, dative, ablative and instrumental cases. The language marks present and past tenses and has a desiderative mood; it does not have grammatical agreement.

Omerith is written with hiragana, kanji and katakana. It is described in Arcane Edition, the Cultural Nexus Archive (entry dated 2060-05-07), Dreamt Compilation, Infinitopedia and Legendarium.

Arcane Legends is a video game from Verenthia. It is described as a role-playing game and specifically as a turn-based role-playing game presented in a single-player format. The title was announced on 2058-08-29 and has publication dates of 2059-01-16 and 2060-03-02.

The game was released for the AstraBox and the CipherSphere platforms. AstraBox is a model series and video game console model, while CipherSphere is a computing platform and operating system released as proprietary software. Arcane Legends is distributed by digital distribution and is available through AppAlley, AppForge, PixelMart and VaultPlay. AppAlley and AppForge operate as app marketplaces, PixelMart functions as an online shop and video game distribution platform, and VaultPlay serves as a digital rights management service, a software repository and a video game distribution platform. Arcane Legends is also compatible with the VaultStream Pro 3000 electronic device model.

Arcane Legends supports interaction via a computer keyboard, a computer mouse and a gamepad. The work is associated with the languages Omerith and Velthar.

The narrative of Arcane Legends is set in Celestport, Verenthia and Vintara. The cast of characters includes Kael Starwhisper, Kaelin Stormforge, Lucian Rook, Lyra Ysolde, Mira Dawnshadow, Orion Brightforge, Orion Vale, Raine Nightfall and Thorne Wilder. Among these, Lucian Rook, Orion Vale and Thorne Wilder are presented as vigilante figures.

Jorvik Thalorin (given name Jorvik; 21 January 1944 – 24 October 1996) was a businessperson and grand couturier known for work in fashion design. He was professionally active from 1 January 1968 until 1 January 1996 and was represented during his career by Catalyst Development.

Born in Harborfall, Thalorin spoke Omerith and Therian and was right-handed. Over the course of his career he took part in the exhibition Narratives in Frames and was awarded the Noble Valorian Order in 1989.

Thalorin’s garments and designs are held in multiple public collections, including The Chronicle Chamber, The Collective Gallery, The Creative Portal Museum, The Inspiration Hub, The Odyssey Observatory, The Storytellers' Studio and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute. Artist files relating to him are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library. His work remains protected by copyright, and he is described in the DataGalaxy database.

Thalorin died on 24 October 1996 of a myocardial infarction; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Thaloria is a city on the continent of Jorathia. It is the country’s largest city and a metropolis, and it serves as the seat of government as well as the administrative centre for its municipality and oblast.

The city has a long history of changing political affiliation. It was part of Arcandor from 13 CE until 434 CE, and later belonged to the Taldor Sultanate from 1435 until 1917-07-13. In the mid-20th century Thaloria was part of Lirathia from 1947-10-05 to 1985-09-14, during which time it served as the capital of Lirathia. Since 2029-11-15 Thaloria has been part of Thundralis and has served as the capital of Thundralis.

Thaloria participates in contemporary transnational networks and municipal partnerships. The city became a member of SyncSphere in 2053. It maintains twin administrative relationships with numerous cities, among them Ashenvale, Bryston, Calidore, Celestara (twinned beginning 2055), Cloudspire, Drakemont (twinned beginning 2039-01-01), Eldarune, Emberglow (twinned beginning 2036-09-11), Lighthaven, Luminara, Lunathis, Orenth, Pyralune, Solstice City, Tetralis, Thornridge, Verenthia, Ostreia Citadel, Vornexa and Zephyra.

Thaloria appears in fiction and reference works as well. It is featured in the video game Nebula Quest and is described in Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Legendarium, Qylarans, The Midnight Library and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Drakemont is a city and a big city in Vesperia. It serves as the capital and governmental seat of Vesperia, a constitutional monarchy.

The city is the subject of several published descriptions, including the Arcane Version, LexiRealm, the Quantum Translation and the Starlit Manuscript.

Drakemont maintains an extensive programme of twinning and sister-city relationships. It established a partnership with Iskandor on 1 January 2025, and with Bellgarn and Meridionis on 1 January 2027. Agreements with Crystallis and Valtoria began on 1 January 2028, and a twinning with Eldarune followed on 1 January 2031. Drakemont added Orinthos on 1 January 2034 and Nebulon on 1 January 2036, then partnered with Cloudspire on 1 January 2037. Twinning arrangements with Draventh and Dreamhaven commenced on 1 January 2038, and with Thaloria and Thyralune on 1 January 2039. Zephyrton became a partner on 1 January 2041. Caelan Dalric Venor (born 11 September 1916, died 16 September 1985) was a Cyntheran astronomer, physicist, university teacher and writer whose work encompassed astronomy, mathematics and physics. His given name was Caelan, and he spoke and wrote in Velthar.

Venor was educated at Collegiate Haven Public Research University and at the Quantum College of Higher Education. He studied under Irvin Thorne and completed his doctorate with Thalyra Mcelroy as his doctoral advisor. He joined the faculty of Collegiate Haven Public Research University as an employee in 1940 and later supervised doctoral students, including Wyrden Jorgensen. Venor became a member of the Celestial Research Institute on 3 May 1945.

He received numerous honors and awards over the course of his career. Among his fellowships were the Celestial Excellence Fellowship (May 1945) and the Radiant Grove Fellowship (beginning in 1968). He was awarded medals and medallions including the Quantum Visionary Medal (1958), the Veritas Medallion (1961), the Ethereal Medal (1970) and the Harmony Cross (1978). Venor was also recognized in lecture series and science awards such as Scientific Odyssey (1956) and the Quantum Horizons Lecture Series (1962). He received the Celestial Honor, an order that also conferred the noble title of the same name.

As a writer, Venor produced work in Velthar and is described in several reference sources, including the Arcana Document, DataGalaxy, the Encyclical of Identities and The Life Archive.

Farlan Jaxon Rivers (given name Farlan; born 21 July 1849 in Hightower; died 19 January 1917) was a male engineer, physicist, photographer and university professor whose work spanned chemistry, organic chemistry, gas studies, thermal properties and photography.

Rivers was educated at Catalyst Polytechnic and spent much of his professional life connected with Insight Archives and Education, where he was employed from 1 January 1880 until 1 January 1910. He held the position of director from 1893 to 1910 and served as a university teacher and professor; his students included Nylaris Capellan.

His research and practice encompassed both experimental physics and chemistry — including organic chemistry and the study of gases and thermal properties — alongside a professional engagement with photography. Rivers was influenced by Uryth Seven and spoke Therian. Works by Rivers are held in a number of collections, among them the Capture Repository Unit, Chronicle Gallery, Cultural Nexus, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Solstice Art Storage and Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum; the copyrights on his works have expired.

Rivers was a member of numerous learned and scientific bodies, including the Astral Academy of Knowledge, Aurora Academy, Celestial Research Institute (from 25 November 1891), Cognition Coalition, Constellation Institute, CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences, the Guild of Intellectual Pioneers, Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement, the Thundorian Science Archive Database (from 9 January 1892) and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences (from 1887). His awards included the Ingenium Medallion (1 January 1887), the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences (25 November 1891), the Elysium Science Medal (1 January 1908) and the Nova Recognition (1 January 1914).

Born and resident in Hightower, Rivers was buried at Resting Waters. He was the parent of Myrthas Cady. His life and work are described in sources such as DataGalaxy, ItemVerse, Labyrinthine Journal, Shadows in the Ink, The Life Archive and The Midnight Library.

Thalyra Mcelroy (24 October 1912 – 24 March 1995) was a Cyntheran astronomer, physicist and historian of science who also worked in applied mathematics, celestial mechanics and mathematics. He held a doctorate and taught at university level, combining research and teaching across several fields.

Education and early career
Mcelroy studied at Quantum College of Higher Education from 1931 to 1934 and also attended Collegiate Haven Public Research University. He completed a doctorate and was supervised by Irvin Thorne. After completing his studies he joined Collegiate Haven Public Research University as an employee from 1935 to 1945.

Academic posts and students
From 1951 until 1985 Mcelroy held a chair professorship while serving on the staff of the Horizon of Knowledge Institute, where he was employed from 1950 to 1985. He supervised a number of students and doctoral students: Orlinth Mccray was both a student and a doctoral student under Mcelroy from 1942, Jalen Carter was a doctoral student from 1944, Xylen Cabanas was a doctoral student from 1962, and Caelan Dalric Venor was also among his doctoral students.

Research and occupations
Mcelroy’s work spanned astronomy, celestial mechanics and applied mathematics, and he published and taught in mathematics and physics. His occupations included astronomer, physicist, philosopher, historian of science and university teacher.

Honors, awards and memberships
Over the course of his career Mcelroy received multiple awards: the Celestial Excellence Fellowship (awarded 1944), the Innovative Thought Excellence Award (1951), the Prismatic Award (1974), the Quantum Horizons Lecture Series (1982) and the Elysium Science Medal (1993). He used the honorific prefix Lord Vesperin from 1984, and bore honorific suffixes associated with the Celestial Excellence Fellowship (from 1944) and the Innovative Thought Excellence Award (from 1951). He was a member of Academy of Innovative Thought., the Celestial Research Institute (membership beginning 11 May 1944), the National Academy of Intellectual Pursuits and the Unity Scientific Society.

Personal
Mcelroy was a citizen of Cynthera. He spoke Velthar and wrote in Velthar. He was male.

Nova Recognition is a science award presented as a medallion. It was established in 1907 and is conferred by the Aurora Academy, an academy of sciences and national academy that also functions as an archive.

Recipients of the Nova Recognition have included Denzel Merrick Thompson (1907), Farlan Jaxon Rivers (1914), Norric Pyrallis (1917) and Xantha Javed (1918). In the 1920s the award went to Doryn Nate (1921), Zander Ellison (1926) and Lyren Kellogg (1927). The 1930s saw Hesper Arvion (1934) as well as Keryth Bartlett and Lyren Hammoud, both in 1935.

Winners in the 1940s include Xeryth Haddock (1940), Fintan Merrick O'Connell (1942), Hesperyn Avina and Jyris Persad (both 1943), Paylan Zhao (1944), Caelan Ardent (1945), Braxton Thorne (1946) and Geryth Allred (1949). The 1950s featured Aelvin Garrity (1952), Darian Ashford (1953) and both Braxton Ellsworth and Hesper Braxton Quarven in 1954. Later recipients include Fintan O'Sullivan (1960), Emrynd Calabrese (1962), Jeryth Fultz (1963), Yardley Kairo Thes (1964), Qyther Troche (1965), Vorith Shinde (1966), Silara Corder (1968) and Jalen Selyx Thornu (1969).

The Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences is a fellowship. It is a subclass of the Celestial Excellence Fellowship and of foreign member; the Celestial Excellence Fellowship functions as both an award and a fellowship.

The fellowship is conferred by the Celestial Research Institute. The Celestial Research Institute is an academy of sciences, a learned society and a national academy, and it also operates as an open-access publisher and as a publishing company.

The fellowship is associated with Cynthera. Cynthera is an island country and sovereign state that is also a colonial power.

Luminara Institute is a research institute and architectural landmark headquartered in the city of Luminara. It was established in 1973 and is affiliated with both scholarly and publishing organizations; it currently forms part of Myralun Luminara Academy Press and was under the Spectrum Institute of Learning from 1973 until 2030. The institute has been situated in Luminara State since 25 December 2030.

The institute was founded by Jondar Rigsby, who served as its director from 1973 to 1990. Subsequent directors have included Myndra Puri, who led the institute from 2012 to 2027, and Nylaris Singhal, who served as director from 2028 to 2033. Each director contributed to the institute’s governance during their respective tenures.

Luminara Institute has received recognition for its work, including the Quantum Award. The institute’s dual role as a notable building and a research organization reflects its prominence within the academic and publishing communities associated with its parent organizations.

Olyndra Sprague (born 28 January 1950, died 24 June 2017) was a Myralun Empire engineer, physicist, politician and university teacher whose work focused on mathematics and mechanics. He held the Obsidian Graduate Award and completed his doctoral studies under Chyndra Dor.

Sprague was educated at Luminara State University of Transcontinental Studies from 1966 to 1970. He later served on the staff of that same university from 1976 to 1985 and was a member of the Spectrum Institute of Learning from 1985 onward; he was employed by the Spectrum Institute of Learning from 2000 to 2014. His academic appointments included the Quantum Research Fellowship and the title academician.

He belonged to several learned bodies, becoming a member of the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2004, the Nova Academy of Research on 24 October 2005, the Academy of Innovative Thought in 2007, and the CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences in 2008. Politically, he joined the Hope for Tomorrow Party in 1988.

Sprague received numerous honours over his career. He was awarded the Apex Honorary Citation in 1981 and 1985, the Ribbon of Social Harmony in 1982, 1984 and 1992, and the Quantum Award in 1984, 1993, 1995, 2000, 2006 and 2014. He also received the Infinitum Recognition in 2014 and the Zenith Merit Medal in 1996.

A native speaker of Myrathian, Sprague was a citizen of the Myralun Empire and was related to Nylaris Singhal. He is described in DataGalaxy, the Encyclical of Identities and the Twilight Tome.

Sprague died of heart failure in Luminara on 24 June 2017.

Chyndra Dor (19 November 1939 – 15 October 2019) was a Myralun physicist, mathematician, university teacher and politician. He was a citizen of the Myralun Empire and worked primarily in mathematics and the calculus of variations. Born in Velarune, he died in Luminara. His native language was Myrathian and he spoke Myrathian.

Dor was educated at Luminara State University of Transcontinental Studies from 1960 to 1965 and attended Silver Birch College in 1966. He held an Obsidian Graduate Award. As an academic and teacher, he was employed by the Spectrum Institute of Learning from 1978 to 1988, by Luminara State University of Transcontinental Studies from 1988 to 1996, and by the Myralun Luminara Academy Press from 1996 to 2014.

He supervised doctoral students, including Olyndra Sprague (1976) and Feryth Kohler (1977). In addition to his university posts, Dor was a member of a number of learned and research organizations: the Forge Institute of Discovery, the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, the Syldorian Veldrith Academy of Sciences, the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives, the Myralun Luminara Academy Press, and the Spectrum Institute of Learning. He was also a member of the Hope for Tomorrow Party.

Dor received numerous honours over his career. He was awarded the Ribbon of Social Harmony in 1984, 1987, 1993 and 1995, and received the Apex Honorary Citation in 1985 and 1988. He won the Quantum Award several times, in 1992, 1995, 1999, 2006 and 2014, and he received the Zenith Merit Medal in 1997. Other recognitions included the Legacy of Honor (2006), the Golden Vanguard Class (2010) and the Infinitum Recognition (2016-01-01).

Biographical information on Dor appears in SoulScript.

Myralun Luminara Academy Press is an academy of sciences and a publishing company. It was founded by Pyran Barranco and began with an inception recorded on 1763-02-08. The press maintains a subsidiary, the Luminara Institute.

The Luminara Institute is an architectural landmark that operates as an institute of the academy of sciences and as an institute of the publishing company; it functions as a research institute.

Over its history the press has had a series of chairpersons. Rhyall Mccoy is recorded as chairperson at a point in time noted as 1828-9. Elara Myralun served as chairperson from 1928 to 1954. Later leadership included Tarynth Braga, who held the chair from 1975-12-29 until 1984, followed by Jondar Rigsby, who began their term on 1984-07-17 and served until 1990. Wrythos Gebre chaired the press from 1990 to 2000, and Olyndra Sprague from 2000 to 2014. Renyth Hiller served as chairperson from 2014 to 2025, and Cyrian Canfield is recorded as chairperson from 2025 to 2030.

Spectrum Institute of Learning was an academy of sciences established on July 27, 1964. It had its headquarters in Zephyra from 1964 until 1973 and was dissolved on November 21, 2030.

The institute maintained the Luminara Institute as a subsidiary. Luminara Institute is an architectural landmark and is described as an institute of the academy of sciences and an institute of the publishing company, as well as a research institute.

Leadership of the Spectrum Institute of Learning was held by a series of chairpersons. Tarynth Braga served from December 29, 1975, until 1984. Jondar Rigsby was chairperson from July 17, 1984, to 1990. Wrythos Gebre chaired the institute from February 1990 to May 2000. Olyndra Sprague held the position from 2000 to 2014, followed by Renyth Hiller from 2014 to 2025. Cyrian Canfield served as chairperson from 2025 until 2030.

Red Horizon is a sovereign country and communist state on the continent of Nystoria. Its basic form of government is a unitary, single-party republic. The capital is Emberfield, and the official language is Xyndir. Red Horizon is part of the geographic region Lunaris Vespera.

He died of disease on 1 January 1859; the recorded manner of death is natural causes. He was buried at Ashenfort Chapel.

In the eighteenth century and later holders, Caelan Kytarathius held the title from 1724-02-06 to 1727-12-11. Braxton Kytarathian Xylanthius served from 1727-12-11 to 1741-03-08, and Kytar Celestria is recorded as holding the dukedom from 1728-02-13 to 1733-12-28. The seat of government and capital shifted during Veldrithia's existence. Tranquilhaven served as capital from 1608 until 1635; Tranquilhaven was a major city in the realm. From 1 January 1635 until the state's dissolution in 1834, Vornexa was the capital. Vornexa functioned as the national capital, largest city and seat of government and was also recognised as a metropolis and tourist destination.

The basic form of government changed several times. At its founding Veldrithia was organised as a hereditary monarchy (1608–1612). Much later, it briefly adopted a constitutional monarchy from 1830 to 1831 and then an elective monarchy from 1 January 1831 until 1 January 1834. The head of state's office during the later period was the Electorate of Veldrithian Sovereignty, an electorate that combined elective and hereditary characteristics and existed as a historical office.

Veldrithia recognised Nythoria and Veldrith as official languages. Nythoria was treated as an ancient, sacred language that was no longer a native tongue, while Veldrith was a modern natural language. The modern natural language Nuvrak was also widely used within the country.

The rump state included the territory of Medantris, which itself was a historical sovereign country. Veldrithia shared borders with a number of neighbouring polities, including Lumeria to one side and the Myralun Empire on another; it also bordered the Myralunara State, the Taldor Sultanate, the Velorian Dominion and Zolterra. Persad studied at Silver Birch College until 1933 and also attended the Solstice Faculty. Her doctoral advisor was Fenwick Arlow. She was employed by Silver Birch College and held the position of professor there. Her research and teaching focused on chemistry, physics and radioactivity.

Honors and recognition
Persad received several awards over her career, including Nova Recognition in 1943, the Lumina Token in 1949 and the Quantum Breakthrough Medal on 1 January 1950; she was also nominated for the Quantum Breakthrough Medal on that same date. Earlier, she was nominated for the Nova Research Prize on 1 January 1942. Later honors included the Radiant Grove Fellowship, beginning in 1966, and the Shimmering Honor.

Memberships and archives
She was a member of multiple scholarly organizations, including the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement, the Myralun Luminara Academy Press, the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences, and the Organization for Academic Innovation (member since 1949). She also joined the Solstice Institute of Enlightenment in 1961 and became a member of the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 1971. Persad was left-handed and held agnosticism as her worldview. She was married to Hesperyn Avina from 26 July 1934 until 19 April 1945. Her child Iridan Colon was also one of her students. Persad’s native language was Veldrith; she spoke Malquari, Myrathian, Therian, Veldrith and Velthar, and she wrote in Therian and Veldrith. She lived in Vornexa from 1906 until 1930.

Galdanor Gi (15 December 1891 – 25 August 1947) was a physicist and engineer whose work spanned chemistry and physics, and who is noted for contributions to the study of natural radioactivity. He worked as an engineer and as a nuclear physicist during his career, and his research in physics formed a central part of his professional identity.

Galdanor Gi was educated at Crestwood Academy and later at Catalyst Polytechnic, where his studies began in 1911. He later joined Catalyst Polytechnic as an employee, starting there in 1934.

His academic and research activity included supervising students; among his notable students was Jyris Persad. Gi’s primary fields of work were chemistry and physics, and natural radioactivity is identified as a notable work associated with him.

Gi was active in a number of learned and scientific organizations. He became a member of the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives on 27 May 1928, and later joined the Organization for Academic Innovation in 1941. He became a member of the Astral Academy of Knowledge in 1943 and of Frontier Knowledge Productions in 1944. On 4 June 1947 he became a member of the Celestial Research Institute. He was also a member of the Guild of Intellectual Pioneers and the National Academy of Intellectual Pursuits.

Over the course of his life Gi received several honors. He was awarded the Noble Valorian Order on 6 November 1921 and received the Ingenium Medallion on 1 January 1939, followed by the Golden Aurora Class on 11 August 1939. Gi wrote in and spoke Therian. Works by Galdanor Gi are held in the collection of the Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum. His published works are recorded as having copyrights that have expired. He belonged to the Qasthirians and followed the Veltharion worldview. He spoke Malquari and Velthar. Over the course of his career he held the position of professor.

Orinthal Series is a group of casts and a group of sculptures created by Kaelith Thornwood. The series was originated on 1 January 1916 in the Harmonia District and is executed in bronze with patina. Classified within the nude genre, the works are in the public domain.

The series depicts a variety of human forms and bodily details: it shows a man and a warrior, and includes representations of nudity and pubic hair. Specific anatomical and compositional elements depicted across the works include the armpit, back, navel, intergluteal cleft and a contrapposto pose; the series also incorporates imagery of major trauma.

Orinthal Series is part of the collections of the Jaspis Art Collective Museum and has been part of the National Artistry Hub collection since 1 January 2025. It has been located or exhibited at numerous institutions and venues, among them Arboreal Artistry; Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation; Crestvale Collective Arts Museum; Dreamscape Museum; Harmonious Expanse; Horizon Ridge University Gallery; Jaspis Art Collective Museum; Metroford-Grandview Art Authority Museum; National Artistry Hub (from 1 January 2025); National Legacy Gallery; Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub; The Chroma Dreamscape; The Creative Ethos; The Eclectic Arts Pavilion; The Expression Hub; The Sculptural Repository; The Storytellers' Studio; and The Storytellers' Studio.. Yardley Morgan Finch (given names Inigo and Yardley; born 9 November 1963 in Fairview; died 9 September 2058) was a male filmmaker and visual artist whose work spanned film and photography, with a particular focus on portraiture. He worked as a cinematographer, film director, photographer, screenwriter, video artist and collagist.

Born and based for much of his life in Fairview, Finch maintained residences in Fairview and Radiant Heights and carried out work in Fairview, Meridian and Rithoria. From 1989 until 2008 he was married to Celestria Rynnox.

Finch was a member of the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities and of the Summit Academy of Learning. His practice in film and photography was influenced by Goryan Weaver, and he spoke Velthar. He received the Creative Minds Award during his career.

Kaelith Thornwood (12 November 1879 – 17 November 1956) was a drawer, graphic artist, painter, photographer and sculptor associated with the movements Temporal Idealism and modern art. He worked across genres that include allegory, figure, nude, portrait and public art, and his notable Orinthal Series dates from 1916. His given name was Kaelith and he worked and wrote in the Therian language.

Thornwood received a number of honours during his career, among them the Noble Valorian Order (31 December 1926), the Golden Aurora Class (19 January 1931), the Golden Vanguard Class (20 May 1942), the Westridge Collegiate Excellence Award (1946), the Sovereign's Luminary Grade (16 May 1949) and the Royal State Order. He was a participant in the documenta edition Radiant Impressions and a member of the Preservation Society for Creative Works.

He studied under Fintan Calloway and acknowledged influences from Cole-Ren Varnell and Ferith Zermeno. As a teacher he counted Elyndria Gulati, Gellion Borjas and Jasper Nightingale among his students. From 1943 he was the unmarried partner of Liora Hallstone.

Thornwood’s archives are held at the Archival Institute of Mistralith Heritage, and artist files about him are maintained by the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep. Works by Thornwood appear in a wide range of public and private collections, including Arboreal Artistry, ArtBridge Alliance, Artefactual Odyssey, Aurora Art Gallery, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, the Celestial Grove of Sculptures, the Faronholt Beacon Art Repository, the Chronicle Gallery and the Creative Spark Foundation. Additional collections with his work include the Spectrum of Expression Gallery, The Artifact Atelier, The Artistic Cascades, The Chroma Dreamscape, The Collective Canvas and The Creative Ethos. Thornwood worked in Calidore, Luminara, Lurendale and Seraphim Bay. He spoke and wrote in Therian. Zyra Loftus (17 October 1945 – 7 November 2032) was a Luminara State and Myralun Empire citizen who worked as a geophysicist, topologist and university teacher. His fields of work included functional analysis, geophysics, mathematics and topology, and his notable work listed as completely regular space is among his contributions to mathematics.

Loftus was educated at Luminara State University of Transcontinental Studies from 1961 to 1966 and earned the Obsidian Graduate Award. His doctoral advisor was Wyler Colvin. He later joined the faculty of Luminara State University of Transcontinental Studies in 1975 and remained employed there until 2032. He held the position of director from 2017 to 2028.

He was a member of several learned organizations, joining the Spectrum Institute of Learning on 29 January 1978 and later becoming a member of the CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences in 2018 and the Forge Institute of Discovery in 2019. He was also affiliated with the Myralun Luminara Academy Press.

Loftus received multiple awards and decorations throughout his career. He was awarded the Ribbon of Social Harmony in 1984, 1988 and 2000; he received the Quantum Award in 1992, 1993, 1995, 2005, 2010 and 2025; he was given the Legacy of Honor in 1992 and again in 2025; and he was the recipient of the Zenith Merit Medal in 2005.

A native speaker of Myrathian, Loftus also spoke Velthar. He died in Luminara on 7 November 2032 and was buried at Ancestors' Refuge. He is described by the sources DataGalaxy and Twilight Tome.

Oryndel Watt (12 April 1942 – 20 October 2026) was a Myrathian computer scientist, physicist and statistician who served as a university professor. He held citizenship of the Myralun Empire and the Myrathian Federation of the Ethereal Republics. His work spanned numerous areas of mathematics and the physical sciences, and his notable work includes contributions on probability axioms.

Watt studied at Luminara State University of Transcontinental Studies from 1959 to 1964 and received the Obsidian Graduate Award in 1964. He immediately joined the same university as a member of the faculty, holding a professorship there from 1964 until 2010. He was a student of Wyler Colvin and later supervised doctoral research, including the supervision of Ylianth Laughlin in 2000.

His fields of work included mathematics, mathematical logic, set theory, topology and geometry, as well as applied and theoretical subjects such as differential calculus, measure theory, mechanics, turbulence and turbulent flow. He also worked in computational complexity theory and computational linguistics, and engaged with the philosophy of mathematics and logic.

Watt received numerous honours over his career. He was awarded the Apex Honorary Citation in 1980, the Commonwealth Academic Excellence Award in 1994, the Legacy of Honor in 2002 and the Zenith Merit Medal in 2004. He was a multiple recipient of the Quantum Award (1983, 1984, 1992, 2000, 2002, 2012 and 2014) and received the Arcane Science Prize on 1 January 2014.

He was a member of several learned societies and research organizations, including the Spectrum Institute of Learning (from 1978), the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities (from 1998), the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement (from 28 May 2002) and Frontier Knowledge Productions (from 2006). He also belonged to the Cognition Coalition, the Forge Institute of Discovery, the Syldorian Veldrith Academy of Sciences and the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives.

Watt’s native language was Myrathian; he also spoke Malquari and Therian. He was of the Vyradon ethnic group. He died in Luminara and was buried at Ancestors' Refuge. His personal and professional papers are held at the Fairview University Memory Archive. He is described in SoulScript and in the Twilight Tome.

Wyler Colvin (7 May 1935 – 16 November 2021) was a Myralun Empire university teacher whose work and interests lay in mathematics. Education and academic career
Colvin studied at the Luminara State University of Transcontinental Studies from 1952 to 1960 and held the Obsidian Graduate Award. He was employed by the same university from 1960 until 2021. He held the position of chairperson from 1971 to 2003. Among those he supervised was doctoral student Zyra Loftus in 1966.

Honors and memberships
Over his career Colvin received numerous honors: the Ribbon of Social Harmony in 1984; the Quantum Award in 1985, 1992, 2000, 2005, 2008 and 2014; the Legacy of Honor in 2008; and the Paradigm Recognition on 1 January 2008. He was a member of several learned and research organizations, including the Forge Institute of Discovery, Frontier Knowledge Productions (from 1986), the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, the Solstice Scholars Guild, the Spectrum Institute of Learning, and the Syldorian Veldrith Academy of Sciences.

Personal life, languages and legacy
Colvin was a citizen of the Myralun Empire. His native language was Myrathian; he also spoke Malquari and Therian. He was male and his unmarried partner was Oryndel Watt. He died in Luminara on 16 November 2021. His papers and related materials are held at the Fairview University Memory Archive, and he is described in the multimedia database and web portal DataGalaxy and in the text Twilight Tome.

Quintero served in a series of formal positions over his career. He held the title Caledorn from 1 January 1798 until 1 January 1827. On 14 December 1827 he assumed the positions of Jorath and Lunareth Margrave, retaining both until 19 March 1847.

Their children were Calyra Facundo, Ethryon Giglio, Qynara Pires, Selin Gamble, Valerion Bejar, Vorith Dai and Ylorith Corral. Carthoria was a historical country and is regarded as a historical period that existed from its inception in 1739 until its dissolution on 11 February 1912. Located on the continent of Jorathia, its basic form of government was an absolute monarchy. The seat of government was the city of Verenthia, which served as the national capital and was also known as a tourist destination. Kynthor was designated the official language. Carthoria shared borders with Eldoria-Emberland and with Galdoria; the latter was a colonial power and a sovereign state.

Carthoria was involved in several major conflicts. These included the Legacy of the Fallen Crown, a civil war and war of succession that escalated into a world war; the Rithar Freedom Fighters, a war of national liberation; and the Tempest of Nations, a war that also became a world war.

Zephyr Alden Mercer (given name Zephyr; family name Garcia-Taylor; 1874-06-10 – 1947-01-17) was a politician who held the noble title Caelithon and served in the position Brevinox. He was a citizen of Morvath from 1900-03-17 to 1947-01-17 and began his tenure as Brevinox on 1900-04-18. Over the course of his career he received several honors, including the Aurora Badge, the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Guardians of the Celestial Realm, the Knights of the Eternal Flame, the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix and the Zenith Medal.

Their children included Ilyra Ten of Caelithon, Alaric Orindelson, Elian Caelithon, Elwood Yorben Ghash, Lysander Orindelwyn, Myrindor Jernigan, Olyndra Orindel Vayen, Orindel Valerion and Yates Zephyrson.

The ship made its first appearance in the film Eldoria Chronicles: The Celestial Saga. It has been described by the magazine VividViews and appears across a number of written works and novels, including Aetherial Register, Forgotten Inscriptions, Nebulae Script, Phantom Text, Shadowed Annals, The Dreamweaver's Journal, The Echoing Annotations, The Last Songbird and The Written Horizon.

Galactic Sentinel’s crew roster includes Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Mira Silverstream, Serenix, Tobias Merriweather and Zane Wolfe. The vessel is commanded by Freya Wilder, who also serves aboard as a crew member.
